title: Are You 'Most Done?
author: Russell Owen
notes: The Caller's Box 2842, permission: full. The Caller's Box's own notes: "Hey can straighten out as it proceeds. Dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey." **B1's hey is danced by the N2 foursome** (DD27, M8b): on a becket set the four of "on right diagonal, hey" are your couple and the couple across the set one place to your right — the couple the transcript calls N2, which becket's relation table names since M8b joined the ends of the set's own loop up. The hey carries the progression, and the author's note is the check. Measured, that one word is what the dance was waiting for: **closure 60.0000 px became 0.0000 px at every checked length (4-12)**, reach 46.6301 px short became 0.0000 at 4-6 couples and 4.0278-4.6375 at 7 and up, and the `long lines: station "1L" has no line mate` throw that stopped eight of the nine lengths is gone. Q12's fixed diagonal is kept; the straightening drift is not built and the strip does not ask for it. **The hey ends short, and the `~` says so** (M9c). Eight written passes with no `~` are *nine* legs - `legsOfPassList` counts the walk home on top of the last token - so the hey danced 1.125 of the weave instead of 1. The weave's four phases are quarter turns, so an odd multiple of 45 degrees puts every dancer's landing exactly on the bisector between two places and `planSchedule`'s nearest-phase search ties at 45.0000 degrees for all four, which it breaks by list order. The eighth token *is* where a hey for four stops, so `~` is what the record meant. Measured, before -> after, at every checked length: **reach 4.0278-4.6375 px short at 7-12 couples became 0.0000 everywhere**, **`progressed` 51.2250 px became a uniform 40.0000** - one couple place, which is what a becket boundary leaves every body behind by - and the collision at 8, 10 and 12 couples went from 0.000 px to 5.571/5.348. **Still owed, one thing, measured: collision.** At 4 and 6 couples the dance is now **green** (9.900 and 9.413 px). At 5, 7 and 9 it is `0.000 px` at **beat 80**, `c0/lark ~ c2/lark`: two instances of one call settle on places chosen per instance, and nothing de-conflicts the choices across them (`resolve.ts`'s `homesOf` hands both the same pool). At 8, 10 and 12 it is 5.348-5.571 px inside A1, which is the same thing a little further apart. Lisa Greenleaf's alternate B2 (#4700) is in the transcript and is not encoded. **M9e measured the hey itself, and the lane was only part of it.** (1) **The lane's half-width was nine pixels too long.** "The lanes' edges are where the lines stand", and on a diagonal the spread *within* each couple leans along the lane as well as across it and was being counted toward the lane's own length: at eight couples the four stand at (16, 40), (16, 60), (-16, 120), (-16, 140), whose two couple middles are 43.08 px apart, and the lane came out 52.3. `kinds/schedule.ts`'s `diagonalLane` now answers the angle and the length off the same split. Measured: collision 5.5714 -> 5.6100 px at 8/10/12 and 0.9635 -> 0.8928 at 5/7/9, so it is a correctness fix and not this dance's cure. (2) **At 5, 7 and 9 couples the hey's four are COLLINEAR.** N2 in becket is "the couple you face one progression from now", read on the set's own loop (DD28), and at the end of a short loop that couple is beside you on your own line rather than across from you: at five couples the B1 hey casts c0/lark (-16, 60), c0/robin (-16, 40), c2/robin (-16, 80) and c2/lark (-16, 100), four dancers in a straight line. There is no diagonal to lay a lane on, and no pass points can be right; the `0.8928 px` is one couple's own two dancers, who stand 20 px apart ALONG the lane rather than across it. (3) **At 8, 10 and 12 the hey's two couples are two couple places apart across the set**, which is what N2 is in a becket set in the middle of the line, so its lane is 86.16 px long and runs straight through the minor set between them: `c2/lark` sweeps 5.6100 px past `c4/lark`, who is standing on (16, 80) through the whole figure. The standing dancer is not an end dancer and the lane's endpoints ARE the two couples' own middles - the lane is right and the cast is two places wide. **Both are DD27's consequence rather than the schedule's**, and the G2 question is whether "on the right diagonal" means the N2 couple (which is who you dance with next, and what the author's note checks) or the couple across-and-one, whom a becket dancer never meets. At 4 and 6 couples the hey is danced by nobody at all - N2 names nobody, every dancer is on hold-place - which is why those two lengths are green. **FR-C1 rewrote what `N2` is, and the hey is a diagonal again (E3, DD49).** The user, asked which four dancers "on right diagonal, hey" means: "N2 would be your next neighbor. in a left-progressing becket, your right diagonal is your next neighbors". So becket's `N_k` is now the k-th couple along the set in the direction your own couple progresses, **one couple place a step** - the diagonal - where M8b's loop row made it two, which is what put this hey's two couples two couple places apart in a long line and collinear in a short one. Measured, before -> after, nothing else in the record touched: **collision 5.610 px FAIL -> 9.192 px pass at 8, 10 and 12 couples**, 9.413 -> 9.192 px (still pass) at six, 9.900 px unchanged at four, and closure, `progressed` (40.0000 px, one couple place) and reach all 0.0000 px and unchanged at every length. The dance is green at **4, 6, 8, 10 and 12** couples and is not promoted, because of **one measured thing at 5, 7 and 9: collision 0.893 px at beat 80, `c0/lark ~ c2/lark`** - two instances of one call settling on places chosen per instance with nothing de-conflicting the choices across them (`resolve.ts`'s `homesOf` hands both the same pool), which is M9d/M9e's gap and not this milestone's. Three claims above are **withdrawn**: that N2 is "the couple you face one progression from now" (it is not, and cannot be - see below), that the hey's four are collinear at 5, 7 and 9 couples, and that its two couples are two couple places apart at 8, 10 and 12. What *is* withdrawn with them is the author's own check. **The Caller's Box's "Dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey" is no longer true of this record, and the measurement says it cannot be**: both becket lines slide one couple place a time through and they face opposite ways, so the two lines pass each other **two** couple places, and the couple across-and-one is a couple a becket dancer never dances with at any k (counted in `set/relations.test.ts`). The hey is a diagonal, as the transcript calls it, and it is not the progression. **One thing to look at on the Stage**: the transcript says *right* diagonal and this table counts toward the direction of progression, which in a left-progressing becket is a dancer's own **left** - so the hey is danced on the left diagonal while the caller's bubble says right. FR-C1's report puts the question to the user; flipping it is the sign of one constant (`becket.ts`'s `NEXT_NEIGHBOUR_STEP`) and none of the numbers above move when it is flipped, because the set is symmetric. The end-effects table has two more couples out at each end than it did: a diagonal runs off the end of the other line, where a two-place step ran round the loop and found somebody.
